name: table
description: Rows of the same shape, compared. 14 uses, mostly in avenID. Two rules ride along: a table that scrolls sideways inside its own region must SHOW that it does, and a header that draws a sort chevron must actually sort — a control that declares `aria-sort` and changes nothing is worse than one that declares nothing.

scroller.$description: The mask is the visible cue. Without it the columns past the edge simply stop existing for anyone not using a screen reader.

numeric.$description: Digits that line up in a column need tabular figures, or the eye cannot compare them.

a11y.note: A real `<table>` with `<th scope>`, so a screen reader can say which column a cell belongs to. A sortable header is a `<button>` inside the `<th>`, and the `<th>` carries `aria-sort=ascending|descending|none` — which must reflect the data, not the chevron. The scroller needs `tabindex=0` so a keyboard can reach the overflow; without it the hidden columns are unreachable without a mouse.
